label: Unit 2
intro: The pretend guesser has only seen the cards you showed it. Give it something different and ask what changed. He can correct a guess without deciding that the next guess must be right.

gelds.text: Correcting and trying a fresh example
Checking an important answer with a person

tryNote: Draw simple cards or use pictures from a book. You play the guesser and say which examples you have seen.

daily.title: Show a different cat
daily.do: Show two pictures of orange cats. Say the pretend guesser has only seen orange cats, then let him find a cat of another color. The difference needs a name.
daily.stretch: Add a black cat and a kitten; he explains which new feature each shows and why the first two pictures left those out.

daily.title: Try a fresh card
daily.do: Call a dog picture a cat. He corrects you and shows another dog before you guess again. Leave the wrong card visible.
daily.stretch: Guess wrong again on a fresh card; he explains that people supply examples and that more examples still do not promise every answer will be right.

daily.title: Ask the person
daily.do: Pretend a talking toy guessed which bag is his. He checks the name with you before taking it. Checking has to happen before the action.
daily.stretch: Use a new question about what he may eat or where he may go; he names the trusted person he would ask and explains why a machine guess is not permission.
daily.skill: Choosing a person for an important answer

goalsTitle: What he should have by the end of this unit

his: Says a machine's guess comes from examples people showed it, not from being alive.
Points out when a pretend guesser has seen only one kind of cat, car, or other familiar thing.
Chooses a different example and explains what new feature it shows.
Corrects a wrong guess, tries a fresh card, and says that more examples do not promise a right answer every time.
Checks an important answer with a trusted person and names one question he would take straight to that person.

weekend: Give him the guesser role. Show only cars, then a bus, and let him tell you which example was missing. Finish with one question he would take straight to you.

songs.title: Show Me Something New
songs.style: Start singing immediately, with no instrumental intro. Soft marimba and acoustic guitar with a playful question-and-answer melody. One clear warm voice, short repeated melody, steady preschool pace, clean ending without a long outro.
lyrics: Show one more, a different kind.
What new clue can we find?
Make a guess; it may be wrong.
People show the cards we know.
Try a fresh one, take it slow.
More cards help; we still can miss.
Ask a person, check on this.
Show one more, a different kind.
What new clue can we find?

basic.label: Cat
basic.note: This cat is one example of an animal.

basic.label: Dog
basic.note: A dog is a different animal from a cat.

basic.label: Car
basic.note: A car is one kind of vehicle.

basic.label: Bus
basic.note: A bus carries more passengers than this little car.

basic.label: Banana
basic.note: This banana is long and curved.

advanced.label: Black cat
advanced.note: A black cat adds another coat color to the cat examples.

advanced.label: Poodle
advanced.note: This poodle shows a dog with curly fur.

advanced.label: Truck
advanced.note: A truck adds a vehicle that carries loads.

advanced.label: Bicycle
advanced.note: A bicycle adds a vehicle with two wheels.

advanced.label: Green apple
advanced.note: An apple can be green as well as red.

advanced.label: Pear
advanced.note: A pear has a narrower top than this apple.

advanced.label: Boat
advanced.note: A boat adds a vehicle that travels on water.

sort.title: Does It Add the Missing Clue?
sort.sub: Adds the clue or Repeats the old clue

items.text: The guesser has seen only red apples; you show a green apple.
items.note: Green adds an apple color it has not seen.

items.text: The guesser has seen only red apples; you show another red apple.
items.note: Red is the color it already saw.

items.text: The guesser has seen only orange cats; you show a black cat.
items.note: Black adds a different cat color.

items.text: The guesser has seen only orange cats; you show another orange cat.
items.note: The cat color has not changed.

items.text: The guesser has seen only cars; you show a bus.
items.note: A bus adds another kind of road vehicle.

items.text: The guesser has seen only cars; you show another car.
items.note: It still has only car examples.

items.text: The guesser has seen only big dogs; you show a tiny dog.
items.note: Tiny adds a dog size it has not seen.

items.text: The guesser has seen only big dogs; you show another big dog.
items.note: The dogs are still all big.

items.text: The guesser has seen only road vehicles; you show a boat.
items.note: The boat adds travel on water.

items.text: The missing clue is a cat color other than orange; you show a tiny orange kitten.
items.note: The size changed, but the missing color did not.

items.text: The missing clue is a dog size other than big; you show a small dog with the same fur color.
items.note: The size changed even though the color stayed the same.

items.text: The missing clue is wheels fewer than four; you show a different-colored car with four wheels.
items.note: The paint changed but the wheel count did not.

items.text: The missing clue is a vehicle on rails; you show a train carrying cars.
items.note: The train travels on rails even with cars on it.

items.text: The missing clue is an apple color other than red; you turn the same red apple picture upside down.
items.note: Turning the card does not add an apple color.

sort.title: Did We Check with a Person?
sort.sub: Checked with a person or Only a guess

items.text: A toy guesses which bag is yours; you ask Dad to check the name.
items.note: Dad checks the name before you take the bag.

items.text: A toy says a bag is yours; you take it without asking.
items.note: The toy guess was the only check.

items.text: A screen names a plant; you ask your teacher to check it.
items.note: Your teacher can help check the plant name.

items.text: A screen names a plant; you repeat the name without checking.
items.note: Repeating a guess does not check it.

items.text: A speaker guesses pickup time; you ask Mom what the plan is.
items.note: Mom knows the pickup plan.

items.text: A speaker guesses pickup time; you head to the door without asking.
items.note: A guessed time is not a pickup plan.

items.text: A toy says a loose button is yours; Dad checks whose shirt lost it.
items.note: Dad checks where the button came from.

items.text: A toy says a loose button is yours; you put it in your pocket.
items.note: The toy did not check who lost the button.

items.text: A screen guesses which classroom to enter; you ask your teacher.
items.note: Your teacher can tell you the right room.

items.text: Two toys give the same answer about leaving the room; you go without asking a grown-up.
items.note: Two matching guesses still are not permission.

items.text: A screen gives a snack answer; Mom checks the package before you eat.
items.note: Mom checks the actual food instead of trusting the guess.

items.text: The toy was right yesterday; today you follow its new answer without asking.
items.note: Yesterday being right does not check today.

items.text: The screen says to ask a grown-up; you ask Dad and wait for his answer.
items.note: You actually asked Dad and waited.

items.text: The screen calls its answer certain; you use it without checking with anyone.
items.note: Certain is a word on the screen, not a person checking.
